cf.title: Backend crash (signal 11) in pg_trgm makesign() after ALTER TABLE ... SET STORAGE on a column with a gist_trgm_ops index

input.subject: Backend crash (signal 11) in pg_trgm makesign() after ALTER TABLE ... SET STORAGE on a column with a gist_trgm_ops index

verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated with a reproducer and a backtrace, and demand is shown: a backend crash on 16, 17 and 18. No objection survived at level 1a or 1b. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is a fixable level 2 point: v1 stops new damage but the thread does not settle how users repair indexes that SET STORAGE already changed. A committer who knows index catalog code needs to decide the repair path and the back-branch plan.

brief.title: Stop SET STORAGE from changing attstorage on opclass storage-type index columns
brief.problem: alter table ... alter column ... set storage EXTENDED or MAIN copies the new attstorage onto index columns whose type is the opclass STORAGE type, such as gtrgm. Later inserts write short varlena headers, and code that reads a 4-byte header crashes the backend. The reporter hit this on 16, 17 and 18, and on managed cloud services.
brief.proposed_design: SetIndexStorageProperties() skips the catalog update when the index column type differs from the heap column type, so a btree index on the same column still gets the new setting. SET COMPRESSION uses the same helper and gets the same rule. A second POC patch from another reviewer makes REINDEX reset wrong attstorage values on indexes that were already changed.
user_visible_surface: alter table ... set storage no longer changes pg_attribute.attstorage of GiST, GIN or SP-GiST index columns whose type comes from the opclass STORAGE type.
alter table ... set compression follows the same rule for those index columns.
REINDEX resets wrong attstorage values on affected indexes (POC patch only).
author_claims: The bug is that the helper copied heap attstorage even after ConstructTupleDescriptor() replaced the index column type with the opclass STORAGE type.
A btree index on the same column still receives the new setting.
Kirill Reshke claims btree, hash and BRIN are safe because those AMs reject a STORAGE type that differs from the data type.
Kirill Reshke shows lost rows in index scans with intarray gist__intbig_ops, and says third-party SP-GiST opclasses can crash the same way.
Kirill Reshke says REINDEX fails on an affected index in the same way as the insert.
brief.thread_state: Andrey Rachitskiy posted a v1 fix the same day, and Kirill Reshke widened the scope to GIN, GiST and SP-GiST and added a REINDEX POC patch. Nobody has reviewed either patch yet, and CFbot reports that the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: No readable patch is visible, so reviewers cannot check the exact type comparison or the tests.
The proposal does not say which branches would get the fix.
The thread does not say how users repair indexes that already hold short-header keys, since Kirill reports REINDEX fails on them.
The thread does not say whether the v1 fix and the REINDEX POC patch are meant to go in together.
The thread does not say if pg_upgrade or pg_dump carry the wrong attstorage on index columns.

objections.title: No defined repair path for indexes already changed by SET STORAGE
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 16 ran SET STORAGE EXTENDED last year, and their gist_trgm_ops index column still has attstorage 'x'. After the minor update with v1, the next insert still crashes, or an intarray index scan still loses rows, until someone repairs that index.
objections.argument: The v1 fix in message #2 only stops new damage, and the reporter found the bug on 16, 17, 18 and managed services, so damaged catalogs already exist in the field. Message #1 says REINDEX resets the column to 'p'. Message #4 says REINDEX fails the same way and adds a separate POC patch to reset the catalog values. The thread does not say whether the POC patch ships with v1, or what the release notes tell users to run.
objections.author_must_show: Does REINDEX on a damaged index work on released branches, and if not, does the reset patch go into every back branch together with v1?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 says REINDEX resets the column to 'p', and message #4 says REINDEX fails the same way. The thread does not settle this, and it does not say whether the REINDEX POC patch ships with v1.

refuted.title: No repair path for indexes already holding short-header keys
refuted.failure_scenario: A user ran SET STORAGE EXTENDED on 16 and has a gist_trgm_ops or gist__intbig_ops index with short-header keys, then installs the minor release with v1. The index keeps its wrong attstorage and its packed keys. They still see crashes or lost rows, and REINDEX may crash too.
refuted.argument: v1 only stops new catalog damage; it leaves existing pg_attribute rows and existing index pages as they are. Message #1 says REINDEX repairs the index, but message #4 says REINDEX fails the same way as the insert, and the REINDEX POC patch is not tied to v1. pg_upgrade recreates the index catalog with the type's typstorage but links the old index files, so packed keys survive a major upgrade too. A committer would likely want the release notes to name a working repair step.
refuted.author_must_show: What exact step repairs an already affected index after the minor update, does REINDEX succeed there, and will it go in together with v1?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. Its pg_upgrade point is plausible from general Postgres knowledge, but the thread does not test it and it asks the author for the same repair step.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Affected indexes already hold keys with short varlena headers, and v1 leaves those index pages as they are.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The fix changes when SetIndexStorageProperties() updates pg_attribute.attstorage for index columns.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Today a table owner can run SET STORAGE and make later inserts crash the backend; the fix removes that path.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The crash is reported on 16, 17 and 18, and the proposal does not say which branches get the fix.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The REINDEX POC patch adds a catalog reset step in REINDEX that must stay in step with the create-time storage rule.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does REINDEX succeed on an index whose attstorage SET STORAGE already changed, given that message #1 says it does and message #4 says it fails?
Do the v1 fix and the REINDEX POC patch go in together, and into which back branches?
What exact step should the release notes tell users to run to repair an already affected index?
Do pg_upgrade and pg_dump carry the wrong attstorage, or the short-header keys, of an affected index to the new cluster?
Is comparing the index column type with the heap column type enough for every GiST, GIN and SP-GiST opclass with a STORAGE type, including third-party ones?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows ALTER TABLE catalog updates in tablecmds.c and how index tuple descriptors take the opclass STORAGE type; no such committer has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: A back-patched change to which pg_attribute rows SET STORAGE and SET COMPRESSION update, plus the repair advice in the release notes. If the REINDEX POC patch goes in, the owner also signs for a catalog reset inside REINDEX on all supported branches.
committability.author_follow_up: Andrey Rachitskiy posted v1 the same day as the report and created the CommitFest entry. CFbot reports that the patch needs a rebase, and no rebase is visible.

priority.reason: This is a reproducible backend crash and, per message #4, lost rows in index scans, for users of GiST, GIN or SP-GiST opclasses with a STORAGE type. The fix is one rule in one helper with no new user-visible surface; review cost is medium because no patch was read and the repair path is open.

provisional_note: No patch was readable, so the exact type comparison, the SET COMPRESSION behaviour and the tests could not be checked. The REINDEX POC patch and message #4 were also not visible in full.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change how MergeAttributes() handles column compression and storage settings under table inheritance, treating them as physical per-table properties. A new child inherits the parent's settings but can override them, attaching a child changes nothing, and conflicting settings from multiple parents require an explicit setting in the child.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We have already discovered with the previous attempt that
there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage.  Also, there
isn't even a patch yet.

precedents_retrieved.title: Vertical Clustered Index (columnar storage extension)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Fujitsu proposed a columnar store extension built on a new index access method (VCI), with row-wise write-optimized storage that background workers move into per-column read-optimized storage. The first patches added a new relkind and core hooks, such as index inserts on HOT updates, with planner, executor and vector processing support to follow in later patches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut's feedback (message not shown) questioned the index-plus-hooks approach and the new relkind; the author agreed that pluggable storage was the better path. The posted patches had no planner or executor support, so Konstantin Knizhnik's TPC-H test showed no benefit, and the author could not run benchmarks without major rebasing. David Steele found too little progress for v10 and marked the entry returned with feedback, for resubmission with a new candidate patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think the patch that was in 2017-01 was given some feedback that put the fundamental approach in question, which the author appeared to agree with.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for ALTER INDEX .. ALTER [COLUMN] col_num {SET,RESET}
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add `alter index ... alter [column] col_num set/reset (...)` so opclass parameters on an index column can be changed after `create index`, using a column number as `set statistics` does. The patch stores the new values in pg_attribute attoptions, checks them with index_opclass_options(), and does not rebuild the index.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Changing an opclass parameter such as siglen without a rebuild leaves the index inconsistent with its options. Nathan Bossart reproduced test failures in hstore after `alter index hidx alter column 1 set (siglen=100)`, which went away after a REINDEX. Alexander Korotkov said the known uses for opclass options all need a rebuild and suggested keeping the options immutable until real cases for mutable ones appear. The author agreed the patch was not enough, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: All these cases require index rebuild to change the opclass option.

precedents_retrieved.title: Custom storage managers (SMGR), redux
precedents_retrieved.authors: Matthias van de Meent (mmeent), Tristan Partin (tristan957)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces the fixed smgrsw array with a registry, so extensions loaded through shared_preload_libraries can register their own storage managers. CREATE TABLESPACE gets a USING smgrname (options) clause, so each tablespace selects its storage manager.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stayed incomplete. Tablespace redo was broken, and the code looked up a tablespace's storage manager in the catalog, which is not readable during crash recovery. The author agreed and planned a file outside the buffer pool, but no revised version was posted after the co-CFM reported cfbot failures in March 2024. In the last message a reviewer asked to settle hook-based versus registration-based design first.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Quite clearly, the current code is wrong in assuming that the catalog is accessible, and it should probably be stored in a way similar to pg_filenode.map in a file managed outside the buffer pool.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fallback table AM for relkinds without storage
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a fallback table AM whose callbacks all raise an error, and assign it to relkinds without storage (views, foreign tables, partitioned tables) so that rd_tableam is never NULL. A wrong call into the table AM API for such a relation would then raise an error instead of crashing the backend.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the patch moves relkind-specific logic, such as choosing the slot type, into an AM that should never be called. He suggested separate AMs instead, for example one for foreign tables and one for sequences. Michael Paquier agreed he was not comfortable passing relkind knowledge into the AM, and he returned the entry because he was not sure what the right design was.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't seem like an advantage to me. Isn't this just pushing logic
away from a fairly obvious point into an AM that one would expect to
never actually get called?

precedents_retrieved.title: Per-table storage parameters for TableAM/IndexAM extensions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a per-AM routine so a table access method validates its own storage parameters instead of heap_reloptions, letting extension AMs accept their own options. A later version extends ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD with an OPTIONS (ADD | DROP ...) clause so options change in the same command as the AM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry sat in waiting-on-author past the commitfest threshold, so Jacob Champion marked it Returned with Feedback. Before that, the test module failed to build on Windows, and the later patch still had compiler errors in gram.y on cfbot. The author called it work in progress, and no version without these errors appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This entry has been waiting on author input for a while (our current
threshold is roughly two weeks), so I've marked it Returned with
Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extensible storage manager API - smgr hooks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a hook, smgr_hook, so extensions can define custom storage managers, with md.c as the only built-in one. It replaces the smgrsw[] array and the smgr_which selector with an smgr() function that returns an f_smgr implementation for a given backend and RelFileNode.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread had no activity for more than six months, so Andres Freund marked it returned with feedback and said it could not be merged into 15. Yura Sokolov's only review asked how an implementation is chosen per relation and suggested tying it to the tablespace with a less invasive change. The visible messages show no reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There has been no activity on this thread for > 6 months. Therefore I'm
marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for ALTER COLUMN SET STATISTICS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops psql tab completion from adding "TO" after "ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET STATISTICS", where TO is not legal syntax. The patch completes nothing in that position.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch and marked it rejected after the tab-complete.c refactoring was committed, because that refactoring made the fix unnecessary. Earlier, Robert Haas suggested narrowing the generic rule that adds TO after any SET <word>, and the author did not want to rework that code while the refactoring was pending.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The now-committed tab-complete.c refactoring renders this unnecessary,
so I've marked this patch as rejected.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 9f984ba6d23dc6eecebf479ab1d3f2e550a4e9be.

It was making the buildfarm unhappy, apparently setting client_min_messages
in a regression test produces different output if log_statement='all'.
Another issue is that I now suspect the bit sortsupport function was in
fact not correct to call byteacmp(). Revert to investigate both of those
issues.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P1] concerns storage settings under table inheritance and pg_dump round-trips, and [P3] concerns changing opclass options without a rebuild; neither recorded reason argues against limiting SET STORAGE on opclass storage-type index columns. The thread points to no earlier discussion of this bug.

The core change restores the documented contract, since index columns of opclass STORAGE types keep their type's storage, and it needs no new syntax, GUC or dump change. pg_dump creates indexes after table storage settings, so dump and pg_upgrade likely rebuild clean values, but I could not check this without the patch.
The fix itself adds no on-disk format, WAL record, protocol or catalog column change, so only the existing-damage path is a concern from this angle.

The fix narrows exposure. Today any table owner can make later inserts crash the backend, and every session restarts; the patch removes that path and adds no new privilege, role or exposed data. Indexes that are already broken still crash on insert and on REINDEX, but that is a repair and backpatch question for other angles.

No maintenance or fit objection applies: this is a crash and wrong-result fix in core ALTER TABLE code, with no new mechanism, GUC, catalog field or hot-path cost. The open points (whether REINDEX heals affected indexes, given that message #1 and message #4 disagree, which branches get the fix, and whether the create-time and alter-time storage rules should share one code path) are review questions for the patch, not reasons to reject it.

The proposal fixes a backend crash and wrong index scan results. The only existing alternative is a workaround, DROP INDEX plus CREATE INDEX, and it does not stop SET STORAGE from setting the wrong attstorage again. No extension or existing setting can prevent the catalog update, so from this angle the fix must be in core.

Demand is shown. This is a reproducible backend crash on a stock install, reported against 16, 17 and 18 and first seen on two managed services (message #1). Message #4 adds wrong index scan results with intarray, so every user of these GiST opclasses is exposed, and the fix only changes catalog writes for opclass storage-type index columns.
